{{short description|Dutch mathematician}}
'''Henk Tijms''' ([[Beverwijk]], April 23, 1944) is a Dutch [[mathematician]] and Emeritus Professor of Operations Research at the [[Vrije Universiteit|VU University Amsterdam]].

He studied [[mathematics]] in [[Amsterdam]] where he graduated from the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1972 under supervision of [[Gijsbert de Leve]]. 

Tijms is the author of several articles on applied mathematics and [[Stochastic process|stochastics]] and books on [[Probability theory|probability]]. His best-known books are ''Stochastic Modeling and Analysis'' (Wiley, 1986) and ''Understanding Probability'' (Cambridge University Press, 2004).

On October 12, 2008, Tijms became the first non-American to receive the 
[[INFORMS#Awards|INFORMS Expository Writing Award]].<ref>{{citation
 | date = December 1, 2008
 | doi = 10.1287/orms.2008.06.20in
 | issue = 6
 | journal = INFORMS News
 | publisher = Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
 | title = TIJMS wins expository writing award
 | volume = 35}}</ref> The award honoured his achievements in the field of mathematics.
